content_voiceover: Treatment of nasal type NK/T cell lymphoma differs fundamentally from other T cell lymphomas because it is intrinsically chemoresistant, largely due to expression of the multidrug resistance P-glycoprotein pump. For stage one disease without risk factors, high dose radiotherapy alone, above fifty Gray, or concurrent chemoradiotherapy is sufficient. When systemic therapy is needed, asparaginase based regimens are essential, since asparagine synthetase is often silenced in these tumors, making them exquisitely sensitive to asparagine depletion. L-asparaginase alone achieves an overall response rate of eighty-seven percent with a fifty percent complete response rate, and the AspaMetDex regimen, asparaginase, methotrexate, and dexamethasone, from the Jaccard study in Blood 2011, achieves seventy-eight percent overall response with sixty-one percent complete response. The SMILE regimen, steroid, methotrexate, ifosfamide, pegaspargase, and etoposide, is another key asparaginase based option, particularly modified SMILE for advanced stage disease. The NCCN table shows combined modality approaches, concurrent chemoradiotherapy with DeVIC, sequential chemoradiation using modified SMILE followed by radiotherapy, and sandwich chemoradiation with GELAD or P-GEMOX. For relapsed or refractory disease, immune checkpoint inhibitors, avelumab, nivolumab, and pembrolizumab, have shown notable activity, reflecting frequent PD-L1 upregulation in this EBV driven lymphoma, alongside brentuximab vedotin for CD30 positive disease, pralatrexate, and platinum based combination regimens like DHA, ESHA, GDP, GemOx, and ICE.
keypoints: Chemoresistant due to P-glycoprotein expression; asparaginase-based regimens are essential
L-asparaginase: ORR 87%, CR 50%; AspaMetDex: ORR 78%, CR 61% (Jaccard, Blood 2011)
SMILE regimen (steroid/MTX/ifosfamide/pegaspargase/etoposide) is a key induction option
Early stage disease: high-dose RT alone or concurrent chemoradiotherapy
Relapsed/refractory: checkpoint inhibitors (avelumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab) show activity
keypoint_voiceover: The exam-critical concept is P-glycoprotein driven multidrug resistance, which is why anthracycline based regimens fail and asparaginase based regimens like SMILE or AspaMetDex are standard. Early localized disease responds well to radiotherapy. For relapse, remember checkpoint inhibitors are a distinctive and effective option in this EBV associated lymphoma.
